unruled:household#1.evidence: p501 pp. 9-10, head of household with a kidnapped qualifying child ("In the year of the kidnapping, the child lived with you for more than half the part of the year before the kidnapping."). Repeats the earlier ruling (rechecked): head of household reads the qualifying person through dependent.lived_half, which refuses on dependent.kidnap_residency (a child presumed kidnapped who lived with you fewer than 7 months, not counting the time missing; fixture stage21.d3.kidnapped_child_refused). A kidnapped child who lived with you 7 months or more meets the residency test on actual time. 'A person can't qualify more than one taxpayer' is the qualifying-child tie-breaker, refused by dependent.qc_tiebreak.

unruled:household#2.evidence: i1040gi p. 13, "Generally, a married couple can't file a joint return if either spouse is a nonresident alien at any time during the year." Repeats the earlier ruling (rechecked): scope.other_income asks about 'nonresident alien status (you or your spouse, for any part of 2025)' and refuses the return, so neither the joint-return bar nor the election to be treated as residents arises.
